bull_bear.body: Priority: Debt reduction and strengthening balance sheet. No dividends mentioned; cash flow directed towards deleveraging post-FX shock.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical (Middle East war) disrupting exports and spiking chemical/freight costs; Competitive discounting eroding price hike benefits; FX volatility on Euro debt; New competitor capacity (400k cum) coming online in H2FY27.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on volumes, defensive on margins; Transparent about one-offs (FX, startup costs); Pragmatic on capex pause.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: DSO increased to 21 days (from 11) due to abnormal March end-sales stocking and higher OEM/export mix, though still best-in-class; Thin MDF capacity is fungible across lines, not dedicated, explaining lower specific utilization metrics; 15% price hike effective mostly from Q1FY27, not Q4FY26.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Reported net debt reduced to Rs 141 Crs (down ~15 Crs vs 31-Mar-26 at Rs 156 Crs and Rs 233 Crs at 30-Jun-25).
- Credit ratings for working capital facilities reaffirmed by ICRA at A+.
- Cash conversion cycle stood at 42 days vs 38 days at 31-Mar-26; the deck says working capital rose to factor monsoon seasonality but is still lower than the same period last year.
- Management states leverage and available liquidity remain comfortable to support growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- India's largest Wood Panel Manufacturer and a pioneer in the MDF industry, having played a significant role in developing and expanding the MDF market in India through continuous investment in manufacturing capability, product innovation, distribution infrastructure and market education
- Pan-India distribution network of 7,000+ dealer and sub-dealer outlets, deepened through channel-engagement initiatives (MITR 2.0 loyalty app with 18,000+ downloads/registrations, dealer meets, 600+ carpenter meets, 78+ contractor meets, 12+ sub-dealer meets)
- Diverse product portfolio across premium, mid-market and value segments giving broad market penetration and customer reach
- New Andhra Pradesh thin MDF line gives entry into the thin MDF category, which the company estimates at close to 30% of the overall MDF market and where it previously had no meaningful presence
- Brand-building push and value-added new launches (BoilBLACK, HDWR Doors, Fire Retardant MDF, Thin MDF) intended to move the portfolio away from commodity-led MDF toward differentiated, solution-oriented positioning
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Industry overcapacity and pricing pressure (Peer Risk / Supply Chain Equilibrium) — Entry of new competitors, rising imports and recent MDF capacity additions across the sector have outpaced near-term demand growth, creating a risk of supply glut and aggressive pricing wars that could exert sustained downward pressure on margins.
- Threat of cheap/dumped MDF imports — The domestic sector remains exposed to cheaper, lower-grade MDF imports from Southeast Asian countries and dumping practices, which can pressure pricing for domestic organised players like Greenpanel.
- Raw material cost volatility — Rising costs of timber, chemicals and resin (petrochemical-linked inputs such as resins, methanol and melamine) driven by a volatile external environment squeeze margins and make pricing harder to keep competitive; a shortage of raw materials could also disrupt production schedules.
- Geographic concentration of production — Manufacturing is concentrated at two facilities — Rudrapur, Uttarakhand and Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh — so events specific to either region (regulatory, logistical or operational) can disrupt output, notwithstanding buffer capacity and contingency plans between the two sites.
- Geopolitical and logistics/freight disruption affecting exports — Geopolitical tensions (notably in West Asia) and rising fuel/freight costs disrupted shipping routes and made certain export routes financially unviable during the year, elevating operational expenses and compressing export economics.
- Foreign-exchange exposure on Euro-denominated borrowings — Borrowings linked to the Andhra Pradesh expansion project are Euro-denominated; adverse EUR-INR movements produced a materially large unrealised, non-cash foreign exchange loss that significantly impacted reported profitability during the year, and the exposure persists while the borrowings remain outstanding.
- Demand-side risk — A slowdown in market activity or shifts in demand patterns can hurt the Company's growth prospects and profitability; management cites premium-segment focus, export diversification and international presence as mitigants.
- Employee attrition — High employee turnover can disrupt Company operations; management has introduced compensation, career-development, performance-management and reward programmes as mitigation, indicating this is an actively monitored structural risk in a labour-intensive manufacturing business.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:

- [Other income] EPCG income was Rs 5.1 Cr in Q1FY26 and Rs 6.2 Cr in Q4FY26 but NIL in Q1FY27, per the deck's own footnote.
- [Digital] New website launched, with 25K+ website visits, 59K+ page views, 5.4M+ digital impressions and 450+ qualified leads cited for the quarter.

outlook.body: N/A (Commodity/Stock production model); Management highlighted 60% capacity utilization in Q4, implying significant organic volume headroom without new capex.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Underutilized capacity (40% headroom) allows volume scaling without capex; New high-margin products (Boil Black, HDWR doors) driving value mix; Plywood capacity expansion possible only after current lines fully utilized.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- For FY27, focus on four priorities: driving double-digit volume growth, progressively increasing capacity utilisation, continuing to strengthen the distribution network and channel relationships, and investing meaningfully in brand-building (a significantly higher allocation than in FY26).
- Capital investment cycle for the Andhra Pradesh plant is complete; management does not plan significant additional capex in the near term and intends to unlock operating leverage from existing assets, which can support materially higher revenue than FY26.
- Ambition to be present in every part of the country from a production standpoint as the market grows; intends to remain India's No. 1 MDF company and grow the business significantly over a 3-5 year horizon through operational excellence, brand building and market leadership.
- Maintain a lean balance sheet, tight working capital and a competitive cost base.
- Continue to strengthen the dealer network, enhance customer engagement, introduce innovative products and expand presence in the organised sector to reinforce industry leadership.
- Continue to expand international footprint through a focused export strategy — strengthening relationships with existing customers while exploring opportunities in new geographies.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Greenpanel operates two manufacturing facilities: at Rudrapur, Uttarakhand (its original MDF plant, commenced 2010, described at the time as the most modern MDF plant in India) and at Srikalahasti, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh (second MDF plant, commissioned 2016, expanded from 2018 into what the company calls Asia's largest MDF plant). A brownfield expansion completed in 2022 lifted MDF capacity by 22% to 6.6 lakh CBM. In 2025 the company commenced a new Third Line at the Andhra Pradesh plant (MDF 3) with 2,30,000+ CBM of annual capacity, dedicated to Thin Panels/Thin MDF, a category management estimates at close to 30% of the overall MDF market where the company previously had no meaningful presence. This new line went through a commissioning/stabilisation phase with initial inefficiencies and higher operating costs in the early quarters of FY26, then progressively strengthened through the year, with capacity utilisation across the company's MDF plants reaching 60% in Q4 FY26. Combined annual MDF capacity across the Uttarakhand and Andhra Pradesh plants stands at 8,91,000 CBM, giving the company a dominant ~21% share of India's domestic MDF capacity. Management states the company has significant headroom for organic growth in the coming fiscal year from existing assets, without the immediate necessity for additional material capital expenditure; buffer capacity has also been built into each plant to absorb demand spikes or a temporary disruption at the other facility.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural outlook for the Indian MDF industry remains positive, supported by rising penetration of modular furniture, increasing preference for engineered wood products, and sustained urban housing demand.
- BIS quality-control norms and the Furniture (Quality Control) Order 2025 (effective February 13, 2026, expected to impact 30-35% of furniture market demand) are expected to formalise the downstream ecosystem, restrict sub-standard imports and favour organised, compliant manufacturers such as Greenpanel; the industry demand-supply balance is expected to improve progressively.
- MDF imports, which had touched elevated levels, declined sharply in the latter part of FY26 following stricter BIS implementation.
- India's transition from a carpenter-driven furniture model toward machine-made, ready-made furniture is expected to structurally grow MDF demand; government support for domestically manufactured furniture is viewed as a tailwind.
- Management estimates healthy underlying industry demand growth of 15-20%, but capacity additions across the sector outpaced that growth in FY26, creating supply pressure, intense pricing competition and margin compression industry-wide.
- Inventory accumulation within the channel ahead of BIS norms, and discontinuation of commercial-grade MDF sales post-BIS, affected demand visibility and reported volumes in the early quarters of FY26.
- Exports remained volatile due to geopolitical disruptions (particularly West Asia) and elevated freight costs, which made certain export routes financially unviable and affected trade flows, especially in Q4 FY26.
- Rising urbanisation, increasing disposable incomes and evolving consumer aspirations continue to support long-term demand for organised building material and interior infrastructure products in India.
- Softer timber prices, improved procurement strategies, better consumption efficiencies and tighter working-capital management supported a gradual margin recovery through the second half of FY26.

deepdive.thesis: Greenpanel delivered strong volume growth (MDF +29.5% YoY in Q4) driven by channel engagement and new product launches, but reported a net loss (PAT -INR29.1cr FY26) due to INR49cr FX losses on Euro debt and new plant stabilization costs. The near-term narrative shifts to defending margins via a 15% price hike against volatile chemical costs while pausing capex to deleverage.

risks.risk: Industry overcapacity and pricing pressure (Peer Risk / Supply Chain Equilibrium)
risks.note: Entry of new competitors, rising imports and recent MDF capacity additions across the sector have outpaced near-term demand growth, creating a risk of supply glut and aggressive pricing wars that could exert sustained downward pressure on margins.

The domestic sector remains exposed to cheaper, lower-grade MDF imports from Southeast Asian countries and dumping practices, which can pressure pricing for domestic organised players like Greenpanel.

Rising costs of timber, chemicals and resin (petrochemical-linked inputs such as resins, methanol and melamine) driven by a volatile external environment squeeze margins and make pricing harder to keep competitive; a shortage of raw materials could also disrupt production schedules.

Manufacturing is concentrated at two facilities — Rudrapur, Uttarakhand and Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh — so events specific to either region (regulatory, logistical or operational) can disrupt output, notwithstanding buffer capacity and contingency plans between the two sites.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and logistics/freight disruption affecting exports
risks.note: Geopolitical tensions (notably in West Asia) and rising fuel/freight costs disrupted shipping routes and made certain export routes financially unviable during the year, elevating operational expenses and compressing export economics.

Borrowings linked to the Andhra Pradesh expansion project are Euro-denominated; adverse EUR-INR movements produced a materially large unrealised, non-cash foreign exchange loss that significantly impacted reported profitability during the year, and the exposure persists while the borrowings remain outstanding.

A slowdown in market activity or shifts in demand patterns can hurt the Company's growth prospects and profitability; management cites premium-segment focus, export diversification and international presence as mitigants.

High employee turnover can disrupt Company operations; management has introduced compensation, career-development, performance-management and reward programmes as mitigation, indicating this is an actively monitored structural risk in a labour-intensive manufacturing business.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's largest Wood Panel Manufacturer and a pioneer in the Medium Density Fibreboard (MDF) industry, with a growing plywood, doors and value-added wood-panel portfolio sold through a pan-India dealer network and exports to nine countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Greenpanel manufactures and sells Medium Density Fibreboard (MDF), plywood and allied wood panel products (98.8% of turnover from manufacturing, 1.2% from trading goods), spanning premium, mid-market and value price segments. Products reach End Consumers, Influencers (architects, designers, contractors, carpenters) and Trade Customers (dealers and OEM partners) through a pan-India distribution network of 7,000+ dealer and sub-dealer outlets, supplemented by exports to nine countries (9.63% of turnover, concentrated partly in the Middle East).

guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Early double-digit to mid-teens (industry pace); Margin: Maintain or improve over FY26 high-single digits (no specific figure due to chemical volatility); Order Inflow: Focus on volume share gain; Capex: INR20-30cr (sustenance only), no major expansion planned in FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Underutilized capacity (40% headroom) allows volume scaling without capex; New high-margin products (Boil Black, HDWR doors) driving value mix; Plywood capacity expansion possible only after current lines fully utilized.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural outlook for the Indian MDF industry remains positive, supported by rising penetration of modular furniture, increasing preference for engineered wood products, and sustained urban housing demand.
- BIS quality-control norms and the Furniture (Quality Control) Order 2025 (effective February 13, 2026, expected to impact 30-35% of furniture market demand) are expected to formalise the downstream ecosystem, restrict sub-standard imports and favour organised, compliant manufacturers such as Greenpanel; the industry demand-supply balance is expected to improve progressively.
- MDF imports, which had touched elevated levels, declined sharply in the latter part of FY26 following stricter BIS implementation.
- India's transition from a carpenter-driven furniture model toward machine-made, ready-made furniture is expected to structurally grow MDF demand; government support for domestically manufactured furniture is viewed as a tailwind.
- Management estimates healthy underlying industry demand growth of 15-20%, but capacity additions across the sector outpaced that growth in FY26, creating supply pressure, intense pricing competition and margin compression industry-wide.
- Inventory accumulation within the channel ahead of BIS norms, and discontinuation of commercial-grade MDF sales post-BIS, affected demand visibility and reported volumes in the early quarters of FY26.
- Exports remained volatile due to geopolitical disruptions (particularly West Asia) and elevated freight costs, which made certain export routes financially unviable and affected trade flows, especially in Q4 FY26.
- Rising urbanisation, increasing disposable incomes and evolving consumer aspirations continue to support long-term demand for organised building material and interior infrastructure products in India.
- Softer timber prices, improved procurement strategies, better consumption efficiencies and tighter working-capital management supported a gradual margin recovery through the second half of FY26.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Chemical costs (40-45% of RM) up 40-45%; Timber stable. 15% price hike implemented to offset inflation, though discounting by competitors may dilute full realization. Raw material mix rationalization (shifting from Eucalyptus) ongoing to protect margins.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority: Debt reduction and strengthening balance sheet. No dividends mentioned; cash flow directed towards deleveraging post-FX shock.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Greenpanel operates two manufacturing facilities: at Rudrapur, Uttarakhand (its original MDF plant, commenced 2010, described at the time as the most modern MDF plant in India) and at Srikalahasti, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh (second MDF plant, commissioned 2016, expanded from 2018 into what the company calls Asia's largest MDF plant). A brownfield expansion completed in 2022 lifted MDF capacity by 22% to 6.6 lakh CBM. In 2025 the company commenced a new Third Line at the Andhra Pradesh plant (MDF 3) with 2,30,000+ CBM of annual capacity, dedicated to Thin Panels/Thin MDF, a category management estimates at close to 30% of the overall MDF market where the company previously had no meaningful presence. This new line went through a commissioning/stabilisation phase with initial inefficiencies and higher operating costs in the early quarters of FY26, then progressively strengthened through the year, with capacity utilisation across the company's MDF plants reaching 60% in Q4 FY26. Combined annual MDF capacity across the Uttarakhand and Andhra Pradesh plants stands at 8,91,000 CBM, giving the company a dominant ~21% share of India's domestic MDF capacity. Management states the company has significant headroom for organic growth in the coming fiscal year from existing assets, without the immediate necessity for additional material capital expenditure; buffer capacity has also been built into each plant to absorb demand spikes or a temporary disruption at the other facility.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic on volumes, defensive on margins; Transparent about one-offs (FX, startup costs); Pragmatic on capex pause.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's largest Wood Panel Manufacturer and a pioneer in the MDF industry, having played a significant role in developing and expanding the MDF market in India through continuous investment in manufacturing capability, product innovation, distribution infrastructure and market education
- Pan-India distribution network of 7,000+ dealer and sub-dealer outlets, deepened through channel-engagement initiatives (MITR 2.0 loyalty app with 18,000+ downloads/registrations, dealer meets, 600+ carpenter meets, 78+ contractor meets, 12+ sub-dealer meets)
- Diverse product portfolio across premium, mid-market and value segments giving broad market penetration and customer reach
- New Andhra Pradesh thin MDF line gives entry into the thin MDF category, which the company estimates at close to 30% of the overall MDF market and where it previously had no meaningful presence
- Brand-building push and value-added new launches (BoilBLACK, HDWR Doors, Fire Retardant MDF, Thin MDF) intended to move the portfolio away from commodity-led MDF toward differentiated, solution-oriented positioning

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical (Middle East war) disrupting exports and spiking chemical/freight costs; Competitive discounting eroding price hike benefits; FX volatility on Euro debt; New competitor capacity (400k cum) coming online in H2FY27.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: DSO increased to 21 days (from 11) due to abnormal March end-sales stocking and higher OEM/export mix, though still best-in-class; Thin MDF capacity is fungible across lines, not dedicated, explaining lower specific utilization metrics; 15% price hike effective mostly from Q1FY27, not Q4FY26.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- For FY27, focus on four priorities: driving double-digit volume growth, progressively increasing capacity utilisation, continuing to strengthen the distribution network and channel relationships, and investing meaningfully in brand-building (a significantly higher allocation than in FY26).
- Capital investment cycle for the Andhra Pradesh plant is complete; management does not plan significant additional capex in the near term and intends to unlock operating leverage from existing assets, which can support materially higher revenue than FY26.
- Ambition to be present in every part of the country …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Exports] "Zero Export sales" during Q1FY27 due to the ongoing war in the Middle East since March 2026 — the deck repeats this on multiple slides as the reason total MDF volumes fell despite domestic growth.
- [FX exposure] The company carries Euro-denominated borrowings tied to the new MDF plant, producing an exceptional FX line (Rs -25.5 Cr in Q1FY26, Rs -1.0 Cr in Q1FY27) that sits outside Operating EBITDA.
- [Other income] EPCG income was Rs 5.1 Cr in Q1FY26 and Rs 6.2 Cr in Q4FY26 but NIL in Q1FY27, per the deck's own footnote.
- [Digital] New website launched, with 25K+ website visits, 59K+ page views, 5.4M+ digital impressions and 450+ qualified leads cited for the quarter.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.

hero.oneLiner: India's largest Wood Panel Manufacturer and a pioneer in the Medium Density Fibreboard (MDF) industry, with a growing plywood, doors and value-added wood-panel portfolio sold through a pan-India dealer network and exports to nine countries.
